chapter: Gillespie and Carter on John Collins
title: Gillespie: Collins in Benny Carter's 1942 band and as a major guitar voice
summary: They met around 1937 and worked together in Carter's 1942 band; before Christian, Collins was the guitar player.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: In what year was this that you met John?
Well it must have been like 1937.
And didn't he subsequently work with you?

Well, he made records with me and we worked together in 1942 with Benny Carter and that was a great experience too because we had two -- three of the foremost exponents of the instrument like -- three. There was Benny Carter, there was Kenny Clark, there was John and then there was Sonny White, and that was a great experience for me too because well at that time I was getting a little name and I was getting a new dialogue, you know, setting up notes together. That was a big experience with Benny Carter, John Collins, Kenny Clark and Sonny White. It was a great

band too.
John was really one of the major voices on the guitar. Before Charley Christian came, John was the guitar player, the guitar player, you know. Of course when Charley Christian came on the scene, Charley Christian had a far western outlook to music, you know, like Oklahoma. So he had that thing and that really set his apart from the rest of the musicians and then he came into jamming with us. So John was really a major voice.
You said there were a lot of important musical lessons as I recall that you learned from him in the advanced harmonics?
Things that he was playing then that you had not heard before?
